name: What inspections happen during a second-story addition?

mainEntity.name: What inspections should homeowners expect during construction of a second-story addition from foundation to final sign-off?
mainEntity.text: What inspections should homeowners expect during construction of a second-story addition from foundation to final sign-off?

acceptedAnswer.text: A second-story addition usually goes through multiple inspections before final approval. Common checkpoints include foundation or footing inspection, framing inspection, rough plumbing, rough electrical, rough mechanical, insulation, drywall, and final inspection. If the project includes structural reinforcement, the inspector may also review hold-downs, shear walls, anchors, and other critical structural details. Some cities or properties require extra inspections for energy compliance, fire separation, grading, or special conditions. The sequence matters because work cannot usually be covered up until the preceding inspection passes. Homeowners should expect the contractor to schedule inspections at the right time and coordinate any corrections promptly. Missing an inspection or closing up work too early can cause delays and demolition of finished surfaces. A good builder will understand the inspection path before construction starts and keep the project moving without missing required sign-offs.
